## About the Show

*Lost* is an American drama television series that aired on ABC from
September 22, 2004 to May 23, 2010. Created by J. J. Abrams, Damon
Lindelof, and Jeffrey Lieber, the show follows the survivors of a
commercial plane crash *Oceanic Airlines Flight 815*, who are stranded
on a mysterious tropical island. The series blends elements of science
fiction, supernatural drama, and adventure, exploring both the
characters' lives before the crash and their struggles to survive and
escape.

*Lost* ran for 6 seasons and 121 episodes, and became one of the most
acclaimed and discussed television series of the 2000s.

## Viewership Data

```{r}
library(tidyverse)

# Episode-level viewership data (millions of U.S. viewers)
lost_data <- list(
  `1` = c(18.65,17.00,16.54,18.16,16.82,16.83,18.73,18.44,17.64,17.15,
           18.88,21.59,20.81,19.69,19.48,17.88,19.49,18.85,17.75,17.12,
           17.20,17.10,18.62,20.71,20.71),
  `2` = c(23.47,23.17,22.38,21.67,21.38,20.01,21.87,19.29,21.54,20.56,
           19.13,19.05,18.74,18.20,16.43,16.06,16.21,16.38,15.68,15.56,
           16.35,14.67,17.84,17.84),
  `3` = c(18.82,16.89,16.31,17.09,16.07,17.15,14.49,12.84,12.95,12.78,
           12.45,12.48,12.22,11.52,11.66,12.09,12.08,11.86,12.33,12.11,
           12.32,13.86,13.86),
  `4` = c(16.14,15.29,13.76,13.65,12.89,13.01,12.08,11.46,12.08,10.73,
           10.78,10.96,12.30,12.30),
  `5` = c(11.35,11.35,11.23,11.01,9.82,11.41,10.05,10.65,9.40,9.04,
           9.57,8.57,9.23,9.04,8.70,9.43,9.43),
  `6` = c(12.09,12.09,11.05,9.82,9.95,9.29,9.49,8.87,9.31,10.13,
           9.55,9.48,9.53,9.59,10.32,10.47,13.57,13.57)
)

# Build episode-level dataframe
df_episodes <- map_dfr(names(lost_data), function(s) {
  tibble(
    season = as.integer(s),
    episode = seq_along(lost_data[[s]]),
    viewers = lost_data[[s]]
  )
}) %>%
  mutate(
    season_label = paste("Season", season),
    ep_global = cumsum(c(0, head(rle(season)$lengths * 0, -1))) + row_number()
  )

# Season averages
season_avg <- df_episodes %>%
  group_by(season) %>%
  summarise(avg = mean(viewers), .groups = "drop")
```

### Season Averages (millions of U.S. viewers)

```{r}
season_avg %>%
  rename(Season = season, `Average viewers (M)` = avg) %>%
  mutate(`Average viewers (M)` = round(`Average viewers (M)`, 2)) %>%
  knitr::kable()
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Viewership Over Time

```{r}
ggplot(df_episodes, aes(x = interaction(episode, season, sep = "-"), y = viewers,
                         color = factor(season), group = factor(season))) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(size = 1.2) +
  scale_color_brewer(palette = "Dark2", name = "Season") +
  labs(
    title = "Lost — U.S. Viewership per Episode",
    x = "Episode (within season)",
    y = "Viewers (millions)"
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~season_label, scales = "free_x", nrow = 2) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    axis.text.x = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks.x = element_blank()
  )
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Season-to-Season Change in Average Viewership

```{r}
season_avg_change <- season_avg %>%
  mutate(change = avg - lag(avg))

ggplot(season_avg_change, aes(x = factor(season), y = avg, group = 1)) +
  geom_line(color = "#2c7bb6", linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_point(size = 4, color = "#2c7bb6") +
  geom_text(aes(label = round(avg, 2)), vjust = -1, size = 3.5) +
  labs(
    title = "Lost — Average Viewership per Season",
    x = "Season",
    y = "Average viewers (millions)"
  ) +
  ylim(8, 22) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13)
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Observed Trends

```{r}
s1 <- round(season_avg$avg[1], 2)
s2 <- round(season_avg$avg[2], 2)
s3 <- round(season_avg$avg[3], 2)
s6 <- round(season_avg$avg[6], 2)
drop_s1_s3 <- round(s1 - s3, 2)
drop_s2_s6 <- round(s2 - s6, 2)
rise_s5_s6 <- round(s6 - season_avg$avg[5], 2)
```

*Lost* debuted to strong ratings, averaging `r s1` million viewers in
Season 1. Viewership peaked in **Season 2** with an average of `r s2`
million viewers, driven by intense fan interest and critical acclaim.

From Season 2 onward, the show experienced a significant decline:
average viewership fell by `r drop_s1_s3` million between Seasons 1 and
3, and by `r drop_s2_s6` million between Seasons 2 and 6. This drop
likely reflected growing audience frustration with unresolved storylines
and the show's increasing complexity.

Season 6, the final season, saw a modest recovery of `r rise_s5_s6`
million viewers compared to Season 5 - likely due to viewers returning
to see how the series concluded - averaging `r s6` million. The series
finale drew notably high numbers, reflecting a last surge of interest.
